Article Title: IPL: MI, PBKS in talks over Hardik Pandya, Arshdeep Singh trade
Article Text:
Hardik Pandya

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: The IPL trading window has sprung to life with a potential blockbuster deal involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh. TOI has learnt that the Punjab Kings (PBKS) and Mumbai Indians (MI) are engaged in advanced discussions over a trade that could see India's premier left-arm seamer move to Mumbai in exchange for the star all-rounder ahead of the IPL auction next month."Talks involving Hardik are at an advanced stage between Punjab Kings and MI. If PBKS part with Arshdeep to acquire Hardik, they could look to bring in a left-arm pacer from another franchise or target one at the auction. However, nothing has been finalised yet," a source tracking developments told TOI.Hardik's future has emerged as the biggest talking point of the trading season. TOI understands that Rajasthan Royals, Kolkata Knight Riders and Lucknow Super Giants have also expressed interest in acquiring him. "The challenge for any franchise is that Mumbai Indians are unlikely to let Hardik go without receiving proven core players in return," a source said. "A lot of movement in the trade market could depend on where Hardik ends up. One deal could trigger several others as teams look to fill the gaps created by such a trade."As part of their efforts to secure Hardik, PBKS could consider releasing players such as Marcus Stoinis and Nehal Wadhera ahead of the mini-auction on Dec 16. Hardik would join Punjab solely as a player, with Shreyas Iyer set to continue as skipper.With the BCCI extending the trade window deadline to November 17, all parties still have time to finalise what could be one of the most significant player moves in IPL history.
Article Summary: Punjab Kings and Mumbai Indians engaged in advanced discussions over Hardik Pandya trade. India's premier left-arm seamer could move to Mumbai in exchange for star all-rounder. Rajasthan Royals, Kolkata Knight Riders and Lucknow Super Giants have also expressed interest.

Article Title: 'Can't see the ball': Virat Kohli, Shubman Gill angry as play continues in rain in Auckland
Article Text:
Photo/TimesofIndia.com

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India captain Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli appeared unhappy as play continued despite rain during the first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday.The match was initially stopped in the 11th over of India's chase of 186, with the visitors at 29/1. Kohli was batting on 29, while Gill was on 17.Play resumed after a delay of more than an hour, with India's target revised to 167 under the DLS method. However, rain returned after only a few deliveries had been bowled.As the umpires looked to complete the 12th over, both Kohli and Gill appeared reluctant to continue in the conditions. Before the final delivery of the over, Kohli smiled and told umpire Paul Reiffel, "Look at the sightscreen, can't see the ball," before making a double teapot gesture.Gill also spoke to the square-leg umpire to make his point, but the officials appeared keen to complete the over. Meanwhile, New Zealand bowler Blair Tickner pulled his shirt over his head, seemingly in jest, as Gill took his time to get ready.Gill survived the final delivery before play was stopped again, with India at 64/1 after 12 overs.
Article Summary: India captain Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli appeared unhappy as play continued despite rain during the first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland. The match was initially stopped in the 11th over of India's chase of 186, with the visitors at 29/1. Play resumed after a delay of more than an hour, with India's target revised to 167 under the DLS method.

Article Title: East Bengal's Asian hopes suffer a body blow after losing to Al Seeb 0-2 in ACL 2 match
Article Text:
East Bengal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: East Bengal's Asian dream is as good as over.Antonio Lopez Habas' side sank to the bottom of their group with a 0-2 loss to Al-Seeb at the Salt Lake Stadium on Tuesday. The Omani champions clinched the issue with two late goals from their Gabonese forward Alex Meye (85) and second-half substitute Zahir Al-Aghbari (90+1) to rekindle their own hopes and stay in the mix for advancing to the AFC Champions League Two round-of-16 stage.With just two points from four matches, the bottom-placed East Bengal's survival is now hanging strictly on mathematical equations.East Bengal's downfall was of their own making and once again in front of home fans, they traded hopes for heartbreak.Habas stuck to the same line-up from the team's goalless draw at the Al-Seeb stadium a week ago. However, his plans were quickly disrupted when defender Anwar Ali was forced off with a hamstring problem in just the 18th minute, prompting the early introduction of Sandip Mandi.Still, hope rippled through the stands as Edmund Lalrindika drew a sharp save from Al-Seeb goalkeeper Ibrahil Al-Mukhaini and Bipin Singh, pouncing on the rebound, crossed it for Mohammed Rashid to miss the target from the edge of the six-yard box.But as the game wore on, East Bengal - who lost to Iraq's Al Shorta 2-3 in their previous home game - looked fatigued, sluggish and devoid of creative ideas required to get over the line.Edmund seemed to have forgotten how to score since his derby heroics in the Durand Cup final, David Lalhlansanga struggled to find his touch and with Rashid's combination with Dani Ramirez missing the usual incisiveness, East Bengal's movements in the attacking third were shorn of sparks.Habas introduced Ake Loba and Lukasz Zwolinski after the one-hour mark and Loba's first touch saw Ramirez take spectacular aim at the goal with the outside of his left boot but the Al-Seeb goalkeeper denied him with an equally eye-catching save.Thus reprieved, Al-Seeb fired an immediate warning shot, but East Bengal custodian Phurba Tempa Lachenpa kept his team's hopes alive with a stunning one-handed interception.When the visitors came calling again, the home team's luck finally ran out. Receiving the ball from the overlapping full-back Hasan Al-Ajmi inside the box, Meye left his marker Mandi for dead with a swift turn and beat Lachenpa with a powerful finish from a tight angle.East Bengal threw the kitchen sink in search of a goal and Meye took advantage of the situation again, ruthlessly exploiting the gap and finding Zahir with a beautiful diagonal ball and the latter drilled it in past a diving Lachenpa to seal the deal.
Article Summary: East Bengal's Asian dream is as good as over. Antonio Lopez Habas' side sank to the bottom of their group with a 0-2 loss to Al-Seeb. The Omani champions clinched the issue with two late goals from Alex Meye and second-half substitute Zahir Al-Aghbari.

Article Title: PV Sindhu concerned over financial woes on Europe tour
Article Text:
PV Sindhu is in the fray for one of the ten elected positions in the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) Athletes’ Commission

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

HYDERABAD: Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu has expressed concern over the financial difficulties faced by Indian shuttlers during their four-tournament European campaign, warning that the lack of institutional support could jeopardise the careers of promising youngsters.India’s European swing covered tournaments in Finland, Denmark, France and Germany. With Sports Authority of India (SAI) assistance falling through, several players had to meet expenses out of pocket or seek help from organisations such as Olympic Gold Quest (OGQ). Some younger shuttlers competed without coaches, while others withdrew from tournaments.Reacting on X, Sindhu highlighted the huge disparity between badminton and tennis earnings, pointing out that players in both sports face comparable expenses but vastly different prize money.“A first-round exit at Wimbledon earns £80,000. Winning the China Open, one of badminton’s richest tournaments, earns $140,000. Lose in the first round? Just $2,000,” she wrote on X.Travel, coaching, physiotherapy and other support costs remain substantial in both sports, she said, adding that she had discussed the disparity with former Indian tennis star Rohan Bopanna.Sindhu stressed that not everyone has access to sponsorships and private support. “I’ve been fortunate to have wonderful sponsors, but not everyone has that privilege,” she said. “If I can find ways to fund my tour. But what about the 18-year-old chasing her dreams?” she asked.
Article Summary: Double Olympic medallist expressed concern over the financial difficulties faced by Indian shuttlers during their four-tournament European campaign. Sindhu highlighted the huge disparity between badminton and tennis earnings. She is in the fray for one of the ten elected positions in the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) Athletes’ Commission.

Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Ayush Doseja, Sumit Mathur to the rescue as Delhi take lead
Article Text:
Delhi's Ayush Doseja plays a shot (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: Ayush Doseja was getting a bit anxious after a string of low scores in the first three matches of the Ranji Trophy season. After a stellar debut season of 949 runs last year, his meagre returns this season could have pushed him back in the pecking order of India’s targeted players. On Tuesday, he maintained his composure to bail Delhi out of a tricky situation on the second day of their Ranji Trophy match against Services at the Air Force Ground in Palam.Delhi were delicately placed at 135/5 in reply to Services’ first-innings score of 266 when Doseja was joined by Delhi’s new crisis man, Sumit Mathur. The two southpaws stitched together a partnership of 144 runs before Doseja fell, caught down the leg side, for a patient 78.Delhi went to stumps at 299/6, with Mathur batting on 80 and Dev Lakra at the other end.The pitch here at Palam offered slow turn. Scoring freely was difficult, but Doseja found the right tempo. He said he had to cut out the extravagant shots to ensure he batted long. “I needed to ensure I didn’t play any rash shot. We had to secure the first-innings lead. There were murmurs around me about my form but I tried to cut them out,” said Doseja, who was put on the BCCI’s list of targeted players. “The time spent with Wasim Jaffer and Hrishikesh Kanitkar at the CoE has helped me understand my game better. There are 92 pitches at the CoE, which prepares us to play on any surface,” he added.
Article Summary: Ayush Doseja scores 78 to bail Delhi out of tricky situation against Services. Delhi were delicately placed at 135/5 in reply to Services’ first-innings score of 266. Delhi went to stumps at 299/6, with Sumit Mathur batting on 80 and Dev Lakra at the other end.

Article Title: Elavenil Valarivan misses out on Olympic quota
Article Text:
Elavenil Valarivan (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: It was heartburn at ISSF World Championships in Doha on Tuesday as Elavenil Valarivan missed out on clinching a quota place for Los Angeles Olympics by a small margin. Elavenil finished sixth in the women's 10m air rifle event and missed the quota by two spots as the fourth finisher took one of the three tickets to LA on offer.The gold and first quota were won by Paris Games champion Ban Hyojin, who scored 253.1 to defend her title won last year in Cairo. The silver and second quota place were clinched by China's Jiayu Han, who shot 252.2. The bronze was sealed by another Chinese, Zifei Wang, who shot 231 to secure third place.Elavenil shot 167.3 before getting eliminated in sixth position. The Indian got off to a decent start with 10.4, 10.5, 10.7 and 10.8 in her first four shots, but her fifth shot, a 9.9, brought her down to fourth position in the first series itself. She later shot some 10.6s and 10.7s, but the top five shooters did better by shooting higher 10s to keep Elavenil below them.Elavenil, Sonam Mhaskar and Shambhavi Kshirsagar aggregated 1894.4 points to secure the second spot in the team event, a non-Olympic category. China claimed the gold medal with 1899.8 points, while Japan took bronze with 1892.6.Earlier, Ela had qualified after shooting 634.2 and was third in the ranking.Sonam (630.5) and Shambhavi (629.7) finished 19th and 32nd respectively.There was disappointment in the men's event as Parth Mane, Himanshu Dhillon and Paarth Makhija failed to reach the individual finals of the 10m air rifle event. In the men's 50m pistol event, the team comprising Ravinder Singh, Saurabh Chaudhary and Amanpreet Singh clinched the team gold in the men's 50m pistol competition.
Article Summary: Elavenil Valarivan missed out on a quota place for Los Angeles Olympics by a small margin. Elavenil finished sixth in the women's 10m air rifle event and missed the quota by two spots. The gold and first quota were won by Paris Games champion Ban Hyojin.

Article Title: Asian Champions Trophy Hockey: India look to continue winning run against China
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

Mandeep makes a strong statement

Fulton wants India to improve after the break

China present a different challenge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Other Asian Champions Trophy matches on Thursday

Match Start time Malaysia vs South Korea 2.30 pm Japan vs Bangladesh 4.45 pm India vs China 7 pm

India squad

India will look to build on their strong start to the Asian Champions Trophy when they face China in their second round-robin match on Thursday. The five-time champions began their title defence with a big win over Bangladesh and will be keen to maintain their momentum against a young Chinese side.India, who recently won their second successive Asian Games gold medal to secure direct qualification for the Los Angeles Olympics, dominated Bangladesh in their opening match. Bangladesh replaced Pakistan in the tournament after the latter refused to travel to India, citing security reasons.The match was largely played in Bangladesh's half, with India controlling the contest. While Bangladesh were not expected to pose a major challenge, India's ability to score from both field play and penalty corners was an encouraging sign.The Harmanpreet Singh-led side scored eight field goals and five goals from set pieces against Bangladesh on Tuesday.Veteran forward Mandeep Singh was among the standout performers, scoring a hat-trick. His return to form comes at an important time, with national selectors expected to assess the players after the tournament.Mandeep was reportedly among four senior players who could be phased out after the ACT.The other three were Jarmanpreet Singh, Amit Rohidas and Nilakanta Sharma.Nilakanta announced on Tuesday that the tournament would be his last at the international level. However, Mandeep and Jarmanpreet are keen to continue playing.Apart from Mandeep's three goals, captain Harmanpreet, Dilpreet Singh and vice-captain Hardik Singh scored twice each. Shilanand Lakra, Nilakanta and Jugraj Singh also got on the scoresheet.India chief coach Craig Fulton was pleased with Mandeep's performance."He (Mandeep) was good, he did full of running and was nice and sharp, which was important," he said.Despite the convincing result, Fulton felt India needed to perform better in the third quarter, after the teams changed ends."We wanted a fast start, which we got in the first quarter. We wanted to play some fast-flowing hockey, which we did. But the third quarter wasn't that good, and that remains a problem. But I am glad we finished strongly," he pointed out.India had to manage without midfielder Manpreet Singh, who has been ruled out of the tournament because of a calf muscle injury. Hardik, Vivek Sagar Prasad and Nilakanta took charge of the midfield against Bangladesh and combined well with the forwards.Mandeep was a major threat in attack, with Abhishek, Dilpreet, Shilanand and Sukhjeet Singh supporting him.At the back, Harmanpreet, Amit Rohidas, Jugraj and Sanjay will continue to shoulder responsibility, while Suraj Karkera and Krishan Bahadur Pathak are the goalkeeping options.India will face a less familiar opponent in China, who pushed Asian Games silver medallists Malaysia hard before going down 4-5 in their opening match.China have brought an entirely new squad for the tournament, with their young players showing promise against Malaysia. Their lack of recent exposure against India, however, makes them a difficult team to assess.Fulton admitted that India had limited information about their opponents."This Chinese team is unknown to us, as they have come here with a completely new group, not the one that played at the Asian Games. We don't know much about them and haven't seen them play. We will have to analyse video footage of their match to get a fair idea about them," Fulton said.India will aim to carry their attacking form into Thursday's match while addressing the concerns raised by their coach. China, meanwhile, will look to build on their close contest against Malaysia and challenge the defending champions.Malaysia will face South Korea, while Japan will take on Bangladesh in the other matches scheduled for Thursday.Goalkeepers: Suraj Karkera, Krishan Bahadur PathakDefenders: Sanjay, Harmanpreet Singh (captain), Amit Rohidas, Jugraj Singh, Jarmanpreet Singh, Amandeep LakraMidfielders: Rajinder Singh, Aditya Arjun Lalage, Nilakanta Sharma, Hardik Singh, Vivek Sagar PrasadForwards: Shilanand Lakra, Abhishek, Sukhjeet Singh, Dilpreet Singh, Mandeep Singh
Article Summary: India will face China in their second round-robin match on Thursday. The five- time champions began their title defence with a big win over Bangladesh. Harmanpreet Singh-led side scored eight field goals and five goals from set pieces against Bangladesh.

Article Title: Nagaland United to add a new chapter to Talimeren Ao’s legacy by becoming first club from Nagaland on national stage with IFL debut
Article Text:
NUSC Stadium (left) and Talimeren Ao

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On the 107th anniversary of independent India’s first captain, Talimeren Ao, on Jan 28 last year, a new football stadium was inaugurated at the foothills of the Naga Hills in Chümoukedima, and a one-year-old club from the municipality played its first competitive match.Nagaland United FC lost that game 2-3 to Barak FC but wrote a new chapter in the football fate of the state that had given India the skipper who led the country from the front barefoot at the 1948 Olympics in London, carrying with him a nascent nation’s hopes in its first international campaign.And, on a chilly evening in Srinagar on Friday, Nagaland United will continue that legacy, albeit after a gap of 78 years, when they take on hosts Real Kashmir in the Indian Football League opener at TRC Stadium and become the first club to represent the northeastern state on the national stage.“Our aim in our debut IFL season is to build a competitive, disciplined, and fearless team that represents Nagaland with pride,” coach Kaizad Ambapardiwalla told TOI. “We want to compete strongly in every match, establish our identity through attacking football, high intensity, and teamwork, and challenge ourselves against the best teams in the league.”This promotion of a two-year-old club into the second-tier competition was courtesy of another club from the region that stamped its authority at the top tier by winning the I-League in 2017 – Aizawl FC.Having won their first tournament in October last year with the NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy title, the club from Chümoukedima got the chance to face Aizawl FC on June 6, who came calling to their neighbours under the banner of Football for Peace and a “Match for Peace, Goal for Hope”.The visitors won that game 2-0, but three months later, on September 9, the All India Football Federation approved a goodwill agreement for Nagaland United to take a cash-strapped Aizawl’s place in the IFL, as the Mizoram club pledged technical and development support.Taking on the baton from a former I-League champion that has represented northeast for eleven straight seasons in the national league without relegation, Nagaland United will look to add another chapter in the football history of Nagaland, but of the football-loving northeast.“For me, it’s more than just playing at a higher level: it’s an opportunity to give back to the club that gave me my start, represent my state with pride, and hopefully inspire the young players back home to believe that their dreams, too, are possible,” 19-year-old Nagaland United defender Thejangulie Zatsu told TOI.“I know my journey is far from over, and I just want to keep growing, give everything I have for this badge, and make everyone who has believed in me proud.”On the evening of October 30, across Nagaland, people will gather around the screens: in community halls, in living rooms, in shops with their shutters half down as Nagaland FC get the opportunity to add another chapter to the story that started a hundred years ago with a Naga boy chasing a pomelo across a mission playground in the Naga Hills.“As a defender myself, his journey means even more to me because I play in the same position (as Amo). It gives me something to look up to and reminds me that where we come from should never limit how far we can dream,” added Zatsu.Friday will see that dream continue its journey from the foot of the Naga Hills to the Himalayan valley in Kashmir.
Article Summary: Nagaland United FC will play in the Indian Football League for the first time in 78 years on Friday. The two-year-old club will take on hosts Real Kashmir at TRC Stadium in Srinagar. Nagaland will become the first club from the northeastern state to represent India on the national stage.

Article Title: ISL: An attacking contest on card as leaders NEUFC lock horns with Bengaluru FC
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: Still unbeaten after three matches, despite the frustrating stalemate away in their last game, NorthEast United FC will be back on Friday to continue their winning run at home and stay at the top of the Indian Super League table.“The mentality. We go into every game with the mentality that we are no longer the underdogs,” head coach Juan Pedro Benali said at the pre-match interaction on Thursday.However, on the other half of the field at Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati, will be a side that is also unbeaten in their ISL campaign and sit on the fourth spot having played one game less than the hosts.When NEUFC take on Bengaluru FC , it will be a test of the Highlanders’ defensive solidity – having conceded just one goal in three games – against the attacking prowess of the visitors, led by India striker Ryan Williams.NEUFC were held to a goalless draw by Odisha FC in their previous outing, with striker Alaaeddine Ajaraie missing a stoppage-time penalty, while Bengaluru registered a 2-0 win over Chennaiyin FC through goals from Williams and Mihailo Perovic.Benali believes that the challenge for NEUFC will be as much about breaking down Bengaluru’s structure as it will be about managing their attacking threats.“The details, concentration and crucial phases of the game will make the difference,” Benali added, underlining the fine margins that could decide the final scoreline.NorthEast United, meanwhile, will look to use their own attacking options and vary their approach to create openings. And, despite Ajaraie’s late penalty miss against Odisha FC in the last game, the Spanish coach kept his faith in the skills of their Moroccan talisman.“I prefer to win 4-3. I don’t want 0-0. I want to win. If there is a penalty tomorrow, Ajaraie will take it. There is no doubt about it,” Benali made it clear.Bengaluru coach Pep Munoz is also aware of the Ajaraie threat to their defence on the day.“They have an identity, some patterns that they like to create and a clear style of play,” Munoz said on Thursday, adding that his team is prepared to face either a back-four or a back-five defensive system.Going into the match after a break, Bengaluru will also hope to keep up their winning run as the fixture looks destined for an exciting contest of attack and defence for the fans.
Article Summary: NorthEast United FC take on Bengaluru FC in the Indian Super League on Friday. The Highlanders are unbeaten after three games and sit top of the table. Bengaluru are also unbeaten in their ISL campaign and sit in fourth place. NEUFC were held to a goalless draw by Odisha FC in their last game.

Article Title: 'Enjoying the game has to be the fundamental,' says Tvesa Malik after top-10 finish at India Open
Article Text:
Tvesa Malik (TOI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For Tvesa Malik, a strong performance at the Women’s Indian Open was as much about mastering her mind as it was about getting her golf right. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, carding a four-round total of one-under 287 (71, 73, 71, 72) to emerge as one of three Indians in the top 10. With Vani Kapoor finishing second and Pranavi Urs sharing fourth place, the home contingent enjoyed an encouraging week at the event.“I think everyone can see it. I’ve always been really proud of how, despite how small the Women’s Golf Association of India (WGAI) started out and how few girls have been playing, so many have gone on to play in Europe and overseas. It’s not an easy standard,” said Tvesa.The progress, she added, has been building for years, with Aditi Ashok establishing herself internationally before Pranavi Urs and other Indian golfers delivered strong performances, including at the Asian Games. The recent Women’s Indian Open, she felt, was another encouraging sign of that development.The emergence of young talent has also caught her attention. Ojaswini Saraswat, who made the cut at the Women’s Indian Open at just 13, offered a glimpse of the potential among the next generation. For Tvesa, however, the key to nurturing young golfers is ensuring that the desire to play comes from within.“A lot of the time, it’s actually their parents who come and ask questions about how they should proceed.For me, it has always been about enjoying the game. That has to be the fundamental. If that is there, the sky is the limit,” she said.She added, “Parents have an important role in helping young players pursue their ambitions, but the goals must ultimately belong to the children themselves.”While younger players today have access to better information and are developing their games at an early age, Tvesa believes they must also learn to manage expectations. The competition is becoming younger and more intense, making it important to balance ambition with patience.Reflecting on Ojaswini’s achievement, she said, “You have to realize that you’re still so young and there’s so much time. Continue learning, ride that experience, and, at the same time, don’t set expectations so high that they become unrealistic.”Tvesa’s own performance at DLF was a reminder of the importance of that balance. The demanding course, known for punishing inaccurate shots and misplaced approaches, requires players to remain composed even when things do not go according to plan.While her ball-striking had been encouraging, she felt her mental approach made the bigger difference during the week.“This year, I felt a bit more accepting of the course. When you play there and you’re from there, the expectations are always high. It’s such a fine line between pushing yourself and almost holding yourself back,” she said.Tvesa, who is familiar with the DLF layout, explained that a single mistake can have a significant impact because of the course’s demanding nature. Accuracy off the tee and precise approach shots are crucial, while missing a green in the wrong place can make even saving par difficult.Her ability to accept those setbacks and move on was particularly encouraging. She recalled how her caddie praised her composure after the final round.“My caddie said the biggest thing was not actually what I had played, but the fact that I didn’t get upset. That impressed him the most,” she said.For Tvesa, patience was the key. Rather than allowing a mistake to affect the rest of her round, she reminded herself that more opportunities would come.That mental adjustment is also central to the challenge she is working to overcome in her professional career. Although she feels her technique has improved significantly, the results have not always reflected the quality of her game.Tvesa, who is married to fellow professional golfer Ajeetesh Sandhu, said, “Your technique is good enough when you’ve practiced and played for this long. Then you have to find the small things that give you an edge. Awareness is a big thing, understanding where I’m making mistakes and why, rather than just spending all my time working on technique,”.Beyond individual performance, Tvesa believes Indian women’s golf needs stronger institutional support to sustain its progress. Drawing on her experience competing on the Ladies European Tour, she pointed to systems in countries such as Sweden, Germany, and Australia, where players receive assistance with accommodation, coaching, physiotherapy, and training facilities.“It’s an expensive game to play, and support is necessary for everybody. Having a team around a player also provides mental reassurance when travel, fatigue, and changing conditions affect performance,” she said.
Article Summary: Tvesa Malik was one of three Indians in the top 10 at the Women's Indian Open. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Vani Kapoor finished second and Pranavi Urs shared fourth place at the event.

Article Title: Mirabai Chanu pulls out of World Championships with back issue; Gyaneshwari Yadav finishes eighth
Article Text:
India's Mirabai Chanu (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Commonwealth Games silver medallist Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships on Thursday, while India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the event due to a back issue.Gyaneshwari, 23, from Chhattisgarh, recorded a combined lift of 198kg, with 88kg in the snatch and 110kg in the clean and jerk, to finish on top of Group C. Her total was also better than those achieved by several lifters from Groups A and B.The Asian Championship silver medallist could have improved on her personal best of 199kg and secured a higher overall finish had she converted two missed attempts, one in each section.Chanu, meanwhile, was forced to pull out before making her much-anticipated debut in the 53kg category. She had been assigned to Group B with an entry total of 200kg but withdrew after experiencing back pain.China's Zhang Haiqin claimed the gold medal with a total of 221kg (98kg+123kg). American Eleanor Ulrey took silver with 220kg (98kg+122kg), while North Korea's So Hyon Kim secured bronze with 214kg (91kg+123kg).The snatch competition also saw seven lifters register lifts of at least 90kg, a benchmark Chanu has been working towards for more than six years.At the World Championships, lifters are divided into groups based on their declared entry totals, which represent the combined weight they intend to lift in the snatch and clean and jerk. Group A features those with the highest entry totals, followed by Groups B, C and D.The World Championships is among six events in the first phase of the qualification system for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Article Summary: Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships. India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the event due to a back issue. China's Zhang Haiqin claimed the gold medal with a total of 221kg.

Anshul Kamboj produced a remarkable turnaround in his second ODI appearance, delivering a disciplined spell to help India bowl out New Zealand for 185 in the series opener at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday.The Haryana pacer, who endured a difficult debut against the West Indies in New Chandigarh last month, bounced back in style with figures of 2/22 in his 10 overs. His economy rate of 2.20 stood out in an impressive collective bowling effort as India restricted the hosts to 185 in 40.2 overs after opting to bowl first.Kamboj had conceded 82 runs without taking a wicket in his 10 overs on debut, as the West Indies successfully chased down a target of 352 by five wickets. However, there was little sign of that outing affecting his confidence in Auckland, where his accuracy, ability to extract bounce and subtle seam movement troubled the New Zealand batters.Bowling first change, the 25-year-old kept things tight through the middle overs and picked up the wickets of New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner and Nathan Smith. His figures also earned him a place in the record books.Kamboj's economy rate of 2.20 is the best by an Indian pacer since Jasprit Bumrah recorded identical figures against Zimbabwe in Harare in 2016.Ashish Nehra was the first to achieve the feat against Sri Lanka in Dambulla in August 2005, returning figures of 2/22. Ajit Agarkar matched it against the West Indies in Kuala Lumpur in September 2006, while Bumrah registered 4/22 against Zimbabwe in June 2016.India's bowling attack delivered a collective performance, with all five bowlers used by captain Shubman Gill contributing to the effort. Arshdeep Singh led the attack with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar claimed three. Kamboj picked up two wickets, and Axar Patel provided valuable support with his spin.Arshdeep made early inroads, dismissing openers Will Young and Henry Nicholls, while Brar removed Tim Latham with a sharp reflex catch off his own bowling. Tim Seifert, who scored 38, also fell after mistiming a pull shot.Daryl Mitchell looked comfortable during his 28-run stay before being run out following a sharp throw from Rohit Sharma. New Zealand struggled to build substantial partnerships as India's bowlers maintained pressure throughout the innings.Axar troubled Santner with his spin before Kamboj eventually bowled the New Zealand captain. The pacer then accounted for Nathan Smith, who fell to a stunning one-handed catch by Virat Kohli.Glenn Phillips offered some resistance with 30 runs before Arshdeep returned to dismiss him. However, Blair Tickner provided late fireworks, smashing 34 off 23 balls, including four sixes, in a 39-run last-wicket partnership with Jacob Duffy.Despite the late assault, India wrapped up the New Zealand innings at 185, with Kamboj's impressive comeback emerging as one of the major positives for the visitors.
Article Summary: India bowler Anshul Kamboj returns figures of 2/22 in his 10 overs. KamboJ's economy rate of 2.20 is the best by an Indian pacer since Jasprit Bumrah recorded identical figures against Zimbabwe in 2016. Ashish Nehra was the first to achieve the feat against Sri Lanka in Dambulla in August 2005.

Former India batter Suresh Raina has expressed his desire to return to Chennai Super Kings (CSK), this time as a member of their coaching staff, after revealing that he has approached the franchise for a role but is yet to receive a response.Raina, popularly known as ‘Mr IPL’, was a key figure in CSK's journey in the Indian Premier League (IPL), representing the franchise from 2008 to 2021. He remains the leading run-scorer for the Chennai-based side in T20 cricket, having amassed 5,529 runs in 200 matches.A four-time IPL champion and two-time Champions League winner with CSK, Raina has taken up roles as an expert and commentator since retiring from professional cricket. However, he is now keen to contribute to the franchise off the field.Speaking during a conversation with his former India and CSK teammate Ravichandran Ashwin, Raina said his years of experience, performances in high-pressure situations and contribution to the team's success had prompted him to seek a coaching opportunity.“I’ve played almost 16 or 17 years in the IPL. I’ve scored enough for us (CSK), played in finals, and handled a lot of high-pressure games.I’ve asked them (CSK), and now it’s on them to decide. It’s their team now – we (Raina and Ashwin) are both retired, so they have to make the call," Raina said.“We’ve done our part, won trophies, and lifted titles together. Now, they need to see how we can contribute to CSK. I’ve been playing since day one, so if they feel I’m capable," he added.The former left-handed batter made it clear that he is open to taking up any responsibility within the CSK set-up. For Raina, continuing his association with the franchise and being part of another trophy-winning campaign would matter more than the designation.“I would love to work with them in any capacity! For me, as long as I’m with the boys and they’re winning trophies, that’s what matters – because yellow is everything to us," Raina said.Raina also explained that he wants to pass on the lessons gathered from years of playing international cricket, World Cups and the IPL to the next generation. Having featured in several finals and experienced both victories and defeats, he believes he can help players deal with the mental demands of the tournament.“I’ve played international cricket, the IPL, and World Cups, so I’ve experienced every side of the game. I know what kind of pressure you face, especially when playing so many finals—winning some, losing some. I’ve learned how to handle that pressure and how to get the best out of yourself mentally. We must have played nine or ten finals together and won four of them. I’m still the highest run-scorer in IPL playoffs, so I know what I’ve achieved in this tournament, and I just want to give that back to the players," Raina said.He also pointed out that while CSK have embraced an aggressive style of cricket, players still need guidance on handling pressure, maintaining consistency and managing their workload across demanding seasons.“They’re doing really well and playing an aggressive, different brand of cricket, Ash. But they still need someone who can guide them on managing stress and workload. It’s not about lecturing them on technique—it’s all about how to stay consistent season after season, and that’s what truly matters," he added.Meanwhile, CSK have made significant changes to their coaching staff ahead of the 2027 IPL season. Former India pacer Zaheer Khan has taken over as head coach, succeeding Stephen Fleming, while Mohit Sharma has been appointed bowling coach. Gareth Batty and Albie Morkel have also joined the five-time IPL champions as assistant coaches.

Modern international cricket rarely pauses to catch its breath, and New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner made no effort to sugarcoat the physical toll on Tuesday.On the eve of the five-match ODI series opener against India at Eden Park, Auckland, Santner admitted the relentless, cross-format schedule has left his squad feeling "a little jarred" and deemed the packed home series decidedly "taxing".Across just over a month, the two sides are cramming in five T20Is across four venues followed by five ODIs and two high-stakes World Test Championship Tests starting November 19. For the two teams, the transition from breathless 20-over night fixtures to 50-over grinds has come with virtually zero breathing room."It's a very quick turnaround. With the travel and the late finishes in T20 cricket, the guys are a little bit jarred.Recovery is a massive part of modern-day cricketing schedule nowadays," Santner said. When the ball stops swinging, and pitches offer nothing off the surface, how do you trouble an international batter? For Shubman Gill , the formula is simple: sheer height, raw pace and steep bounce.On the eve of India’s opening ODI against New Zealand at the Eden Park, Auckland, the Indian skipper laid bare the blueprint behind India’s recent pace-bowling auditions, pegging tall, hit-the-deck quicks as a core priority with an eye on the 2027 World Cup in South Africa."When the ball gets old, when there is not much seam or swing movement, then how do you challenge the batter?" Gill said. "You can challenge the batter either if there is something in the wicket...or you can challenge the batter with pace and bounce."In recent times, several towering fast bowlers including Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana and newcomer Gurnoor Brar have represented India in the 50-over scheme of things. "Identifying the kind of bowlers that can make run-scoring difficult for the batters and that can give us the best opportunity to take wickets in the middle overs — that has been the thinking around trying someone like a Gurnoor or a Prasidh, which gives us a bit more than someone who is bowling at maybe 135 (kph) when the wicket is flat."I have played in the middle overs a lot, and I have seen that if those bowlers can hit the right areas — obviously hitting the right areas is the key — if tall fast bowlers can hit the right areas, it is a lot more difficult to score runs than someone who is bowling at 130-135. You have to be really precise with your shot-making. You have to be really on top of your game to be able to score against someone who is 140-plus and who is 6'1", 6'2", 6'3". There is a lot more risk when you are trying to score freely against that kind of bowler," Gill said.One big concern for India in the lead-up to the 2027 World Cup is the fitness of their key seam-bowling allrounder Hardik Pandya , who has been out of action since IPL 2026 thanks to a series of injuries and niggles.Calling Hardik's skill set difficult to replace, Gill said the team had remained in touch with him and hoped he would return to domestic cricket before making his comeback to the national side."Firstly, he is a great player," Gill stressed. "The qualities that he brings to the team, not many players in the world possess those qualities, to be able to have a fast-bowling allrounder who can bowl (in any phase) of the game, with the new ball, middle overs and death overs; and the kind of batting he has. Hopefully, we will see him back in the side soon."The captain, however, would have preferred a different arrangement for the New Zealand tour, with the ODI series sandwiched between the T20Is and two Tests. The tight turnaround means several members of the Test squad, including Gill, will miss the fourth and fifth ODIs. Jasprit Bumrah, meanwhile, has been rested for the entire ODI series.With the ODI World Cup and the World Test Championship final both scheduled for 2027, Gill felt India could have benefited from having their strongest available combinations for both formats in the ongoing tour."If it was in my hands and all the players were fit, I would have liked to have all the players we are looking at playing during the World Cup for the full ODI series. But the two Test matches are also very important," he said.

Batting stars Shubman Gill , Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul are back in the mix, while Mohammed Siraj is set to strengthen the pace attack. Their first challenge in th first ODI against New Zealand on Wednesday, though, will be to figure out a ground where the boundaries can be as misleading as the bounce on offer.Eden Park is not your typical cricket ground. It is small, oddly shaped and has dimensions that can leave captains and bowlers scratching their heads. A shot that clears the rope comfortably in one direction might not travel nearly as far in another. For batters, that means knowing which side to target. For bowlers, it is about getting their lengths right and not allowing the short boundaries to dictate their plans.The short boundaries do tempt the batters into mindless slogging, but the pitch usually tells a much sterner story.Eden Park's drop-in tracks are lively and offer steep, tennis-ball bounce. In many ways, it serves as an early, unscripted dress rehearsal for the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, where steep lift and seam movement is bound to test Indian techniques. Surviving isn't just about clearing the straight boundary, it's about riding the bounce and respecting the new ball."Ground dimensions is always one to play into your mind at Eden Park.Traditionally, there's a little bit of bounce, which, you know, is good for the seamers. And it can be quite swirly with the wind, which can make it quite a tough catching ground," New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said on Tuesday.The wind, in particular, could make life difficult for fielders, especially in the deep. And there is another factor that skipper Gill will be watching closely.The ODIs are scheduled to start at 3pm local time, later than what teams are accustomed to at this venue.Gill was candid about the unfamiliar conditions. "It is my first time that we are playing so late, we are playing at 3pm, so in the second innings, when we are bowling or batting, I don't know what the conditions will be like, and when you play with two new balls, at night it is possible that there is more swing, more bounce, more seam, and that will be very interesting," the India captain said.India's team combination will look considerably different from the one that featured in the T20I series. Rohit and Gill are bound to open, with Kohli, Shreyas Iyer and KL Rahul giving the middle order considerable experience. Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.

The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Article Title: Jesús de Miguel death: 'Deeply upset' Jesús Owono reportedly seeks to apologise as criminal proceedings deemed unlikely
Article Text:
Jesús Owono reportedly hopes to apologise privately to Jesús de Miguel’s family, as Spanish prosecutors indicate criminal proceedings are unlikely following the fatal collision.

What happened during Tenerife vs Andorra?

Jesús de Miguel lies on the ground after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a soccer match in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Spain, Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (AP Photo)

Jesús de Miguel dies after his condition deteriorates in hospital

CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel Alameda has died at the age of 30 after suffering a serious injury during Monday’s match against FC Andorra. (Image credit: EuroFoot _X)

Why have Spanish police opened a homicide investigation ?

What punishment could Jesús Owono face?

AS

Owono reportedly wants to apologise as Tenerife prepares tribute

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Spanish police have opened an investigation after Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died following a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a second-division match. The 30-year-old suffered a cardiac arrest on the pitch and died in hospital the following morning, prompting a judicial inquiry and questions about the possible sporting and criminal consequences for the goalkeeper.The incident occurred on Monday, November 2, during a Spanish Segunda División fixture between CD Tenerife and FC Andorra at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium in Santa Cruz de Tenerife. The match had been postponed by 24 hours because of the risk of torrential rain, and the teams were level at 2-2 when the collision happened in the 96th minute.A long ball was played forward from the Tenerife half, with De Miguel chasing it towards the Andorra goal. Owono, the 25-year-old goalkeeper, came a considerable distance out of his penalty area to challenge for the ball near the halfway line. He jumped towards the striker with his right knee raised and struck De Miguel in the chest.The Tenerife forward immediately collapsed, leaving players from both teams calling for medical assistance.Owono received a straight red card from referee Manuel Ángel Pérez Hernández, while medical staff attended to De Miguel on the pitch. The striker was eventually taken away on a stretcher and transported by ambulance to the Hospital Universitario Nuestra Señora de Candelaria.According to reports, De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest during the incident, with medical personnel managing to restore his pulse in the ambulance. The match was subsequently abandoned after the referee consulted both teams' captains and officials, who said they were not in a condition to continue playing.The referee's report later recorded that the collision occurred while the ball was being contested. It also stated that Owono had been sent off for making contact with an opponent with his leg raised and using excessive force.Tenerife initially offered some hope after confirming that De Miguel had been admitted to hospital, describing his condition as stable despite the severity of his injuries. He remained unconscious and was placed in intensive care, but his neurological condition deteriorated during the early hours of Tuesday, November 3.The club confirmed his death at approximately 8am local time. De Miguel was 30.In its statement, Tenerife said: “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true. There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.“We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones…that today weep for this cruel outcome.“The family of Jesús de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments.”The striker's death was confirmed after his teammates, coaching staff and club officials had spent the morning at the hospital awaiting updates. His body is due to be transported to mainland Spain for his funeral in Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo.Spain's National Police opened an investigation into De Miguel's death on Tuesday, with the Homicide Group in Santa Cruz de Tenerife examining the circumstances surrounding the collision. The case is under judicial supervision, and prosecutors have also opened preliminary proceedings.The High Court of Justice of the Canary Islands explained that an investigation is automatically opened when a person dies from a cause that is not considered natural, including an accident. The procedure is known in Spain as a judicial death investigation.A statement from the court said: “Every death that does not have a natural cause — what is known as 'judicial death,' whether due to accident or other causes — entails the opening of a judicial investigation ex officio, as is the case here.”The opening of those proceedings does not establish that a crime has been committed or that Owono is criminally responsible for De Miguel's death. The investigation is intended to establish what happened and whether there is evidence of responsibility beyond the sporting rules governing the incident.José Luis Sánchez-Jáuregui, the chief prosecutor of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, told the Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings were unlikely because the collision occurred during a passage of play. He referred to longstanding Spanish Supreme Court doctrine, under which injuries sustained during sporting activity are generally not punishable unless there has been an assault outside the normal course of play, such as an intentional attack during a stoppage.Sánchez-Jáuregui said it was “very difficult” for a criminal case to proceed, but stressed that the referee's report and the findings of the Sports Disciplinary Committee would first have to be considered. Investigators will examine the available footage and gather evidence, including statements from Owono and medical personnel involved in treating De Miguel.The investigation has two separate tracks: the judicial process examining possible criminal responsibility and the sporting disciplinary proceedings arising from the challenge.Under the Spanish football disciplinary framework, a serious incident involving violent conduct and excessive force can lead to a substantial suspension. Reports bydescribed the relevant sanction for violent conduct towards an opponent causing serious injury or harm as a suspension of between four and 12 matches.The Sports Disciplinary Committee will assess the referee's report alongside video footage of the collision before deciding whether further punishment is warranted. The referee's description of the incident is particularly relevant because he recorded that the ball was still in dispute when Owono made contact with De Miguel.The legal question is different. Sánchez-Jáuregui said the authorities would need to establish whether the challenge amounted to dangerous or very dangerous play and, crucially, whether Owono intended to cause harm. He noted that Spanish legal precedent generally protects actions arising from the normal conduct of a sporting contest, while leaving room for criminal proceedings where an intentional assault occurs outside that contextHowever, criminal liability is not necessarily limited to cases involving deliberate intent. Article 142 of the Spanish Penal Code covers negligent homicide, distinguishing between gross and less serious negligence. If investigators establish gross negligence, the offence carries a potential prison sentence of one to four years, while less serious negligence can attract a fine of three to 18 months. Whether either provision could apply would depend on the circumstances of the collision and whether Owono's actions went beyond the risks ordinarily associated with competitive football. No finding of criminal responsibility has been made, and the prosecutor has indicated that criminal proceedings are unlikely. The police investigation remains open.Owono has been described by people close to FC Andorra as deeply affected by what happened. The goalkeeper, who represents Equatorial Guinea internationally, reportedly returned to Barcelona with his teammates after the match and subsequently closed his social media accounts following a wave of abusive messages and chants from Tenerife supporters.Footage from the stadium showed some fans confronting him as he left the pitch, with supporters shouting “murderer”. According to journalist Iván Álvarez, speaking on COPE radio before De Miguel's death was announced, Owono intended to contact the striker's family and apologise privately.Álvarez said: “Some of the people who were at the stadium and some messages I exchanged with players told me it's the hardest thing they've ever experienced on a football pitch.”He added that Owono was “very upset” and that “no one would ever think of someone wanting to harm a fellow professional in that way”.Álvarez also relayed Andorra's position on the incident: “Andorra emphasises that there was no ill intent at any point, acknowledging that it was a mistimed outburst, an action that went terribly wrong and, I would say, excessive and violent, but they insist there was no intention to cause harm.”He said Owono wanted to contact De Miguel's relatives “when the time is right”, adding that the goalkeeper preferred to speak to them privately before making any public statement.Meanwhile, supporters have gathered outside the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium, leaving flowers, candles and messages at Gate 8 in memory of the striker. Tenerife has invited supporters and residents of the island to attend a tribute at the stadium on Saturday at 6pm.The Tenerife Island Council has also declared an official day of mourning, with the island's flag to fly at half-mast.UEFA has called for moments of silence at matches during the week, while clubs including Barcelona and Real Madrid have issued tributes. De Miguel's death has also prompted the Spanish football authorities to postpone scheduled midweek Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches.
Article Summary: CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel Alameda has died at the age of 30 after suffering a serious injury during Monday’s match against FC Andorra. The 30-year-old suffered a cardiac arrest on the pitch and died in hospital the following morning. Spanish police have opened an investigation into De Miguel's death.

Article Title: Tenerife striker’s death after on-field collision a painful reminder for Indian football fans
Article Text:
CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died after colliding with a rival player during a Spanish second- division match Monday

Panaji: CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died after colliding with a rival player during a Spanish second- division match Monday.The 30-year-old, who was chasing a pass on the break into the rival half, collided heavily with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his penalty area, and suffered head and chest injuries. The striker received treatment on the pitch for about 15 minutes before being taken to hospital.The goalkeeper was sent off, and the match was abandoned due to the seriousness of the injury.Tenerife initially said De Miguel’s “situation is stable but remains serious.” His condition worsened and he was pronounced dead early Tuesday morning.“Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, we at CD Tenerife announce the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” the club said in a statement on Tuesday. “There are no words of comfort. There is absolutely nothing that can ease this overwhelming sense of sadness.”When the incident occurred, Tenerife and Andorra were tied 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time. De Miguel chased a long ball that was lobbed into the opposite half but clashed with Owono, who had raced towards the halfway mark. The goalkeeper’s knee appeared to collide with the striker after which he fell, and lay motionless on the pitch.The incident will be a painful reminder for Indian football fans of a similar on-field clash, and death, when Dempo SC striker Cristiano Junior collided with Mohun Bagan goalkeeper Subrata Paul in the final of the Federation Cup in 2004. The match continued for the remaining 12 minutes while the Brazilian was taken to the hospital, where he was declared brought dead.Hailing from Madrid, De Miguel started his career at Leganes and went on to play for eight different lower-division clubs in Spain. He signed for Tenerife at the start of the 2025-26 season and scored 11 league goals in his first year, helping Tenerife win a long-awaited promotion to the Segunda Division.At the start of the season, he attracted interest from Mohun Bagan SG. The former Indian Super League champions and among the biggest spenders in India were on the hunt for a top-notch striker following the departure of former Australian World Cupper Jason Cummings.“We had a call with Jesus and his representative,” a senior Bagan official told TOI. “He said he was keen to come to India but there were two years remaining on his existing contract with Tenerife, so we could not make the transfer work. Jesus has scored consistently in the lower divisions in Spain and would have clicked in ISL.”Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. They said on Tuesday that proceedings were opened and prosecutors will also be involved.Andorra, which is owned by former Barcelona star Gerard Pique, also offered its condolences, along with other clubs, the Spanish soccer federation and La Liga. “We wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace,” Andorra said in a statement.The Real Madrid players held a minute’s silence for De Miguel during training, while Espanyol postponed the presentation of their new coach.
Article Summary: CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died after colliding with a rival player during a Spanish second- division match Monday. The 30-year-old, who was chasing a pass on the break into the rival half, collided heavily with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono. The goalkeeper was sent off, and the match was abandoned due to the seriousness of the injury.

Article Title: 'There are no words': Messi, Mbappé lead football's tributes to Jesús de Miguel after fatal on-field collision
