The football world has been left mourning the death of Spanish forward Jesús de Miguel, with Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé and Gerard Piqué among the prominent names to pay tribute to the 30-year-old following his tragic death after an on-field collision during a second-division match.De Miguel, who played for CD Tenerife, suffered a cardiac arrest after colliding with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during Monday's match. His club confirmed his death on Tuesday, triggering an outpouring of condolences from players, clubs and football authorities across the world.Former Barcelona defender Piqué expressed his grief in a post on X, writing: “I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesús.”Real Madrid forward Mbappé also reacted to the news, posting: “So much sadness. There are no words.”Argentina great Messi shared his condolences on Instagram, saying: “There are no words. My condolences and lots of strength to all his family and friends.”English clubs Manchester United and Liverpool also joined the tributes, offering their condolences on social media.The tragedy prompted several gestures of remembrance across Spanish football.Real Madrid players observed a minute's silence for De Miguel during training, while Espanyol postponed the presentation of its new coach as a mark of respect.FC Andorra, owned by Piqué, also issued a statement expressing its condolences to the forward's family, teammates and club.“We wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace,” the club said.Tenerife, meanwhile, said it was heartbroken by the loss.“There are no words of comfort,” the club's statement read. “There is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow. We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire Tenerife community.”The Spanish football federation also postponed two Copa del Rey matches and one Copa de la Reina fixture scheduled for Tuesday.The incident occurred in the closing stages of Tenerife's match against Andorra, which was tied 2-2. De Miguel was attempting to reach a long ball near the halfway line when Owono rushed out of his penalty area to challenge for it.The goalkeeper collided with the forward, striking him in the chest with his knee. De Miguel initially remained on his knees, clutching his torso, before falling onto his back. Medical personnel attended to him for several minutes before he was taken to hospital by ambulance.Owono was shown a straight red card but turned back towards the incident after initially walking away, joining other players rushing to check on De Miguel. The match was abandoned in the seventh minute of stoppage time.Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation. The investigation does not, by itself, establish criminal responsibility.Owono's Instagram account, which had nearly 30,000 followers, was deactivated on Tuesday after he faced online abuse.A Madrid native, De Miguel began his senior career with Leganés B in 2015 before representing several lower-division Spanish clubs. He joined Tenerife last year and is survived by his wife and daughter, according to Spanish media.His death has once again brought attention to the rare but devastating risks of serious on-field collisions in football.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé and Gerard Piqué pay tribute to Jesús de Miguel. Tenerife forward died after an on-field collision during a second-division match. De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after colliding with FC Andorra goalkeeper.

Article Title: 'We are heartbroken': UEFA mourns Jesús de Miguel; police probe possible involuntary manslaughter

Spanish football is mourning the death of CD Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, who passed away aged 30 after suffering serious injuries in an on-field collision during a second-division match against FC Andorra on Monday. UEFA and several football organisations have expressed their grief, while Spanish police have opened an investigation into the incident.UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin offered his condolences to De Miguel's family, teammates and everyone associated with the club."We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," Ceferin said in a statement. "We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his teammates, everyone at CD Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss," he added.The incident took place in the closing stages of Monday's match at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez. De Miguel was challenging for the ball near midfield when he collided with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who struck him in the chest.The 30-year-old suffered serious head and chest injuries and was left motionless on the pitch. Medical staff rushed to help him before he was taken to the University Hospital of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria.He reportedly suffered a cardiac arrest but was revived by medical personnel.Although his condition was initially described as stable but serious, his neurological condition worsened on Tuesday morning. He passed away at 8 am local time. The match was abandoned following the incident, and Owono was shown a straight red card.Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter, with prosecutors also expected to be involved.Tenerife announced his death in an emotional statement, asking for privacy for his family. The Royal Spanish Football Federation also offered its condolences.De Miguel had played for several lower-division Spanish clubs before joining Tenerife and helped the team earn promotion to the Segunda Division last season.UEFA has announced that all its matches this week will observe a moment of silence in his memory.
Article Summary: CD Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel dies after on-field collision. The 30-year- old suffered serious head and chest injuries on Monday. UEFA and several football organisations have expressed their grief. Spanish police have opened an investigation into the incident.UEFA announces that all its matches this week will observe a moment of silence.
